title: The napkins
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Gully's napkins have been piling up on the shack's counter for three years: walruses, gulls, the uncle, a crab in a hat. The uncle keeps them under the register. Wood finds the stack. Sixty. He's never been jealous of a napkin before.

panels.composition: The shack. The register lifted. Under it, a stack of napkins, ballpoint. WOOD lifting them. GULLY at the tank, not seeing. The UNCLE in the chair outside.

image.prompt: a young man lifting a stack of ballpoint-drawn paper napkins from beneath a bait shack's register while a teenager works at a bait tank, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The napkins fanned: a walrus, a gull, the uncle in three strokes, a crab in a hat, a dog that is exactly the dog.

image.prompt: close on a fan of paper napkins with ballpoint drawings of a walrus, a gull, an old man, a crab in a hat and a small dog, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood. His face. A thing he hasn't felt about a napkin.

image.prompt: a young man's face looking at napkin drawings with an expression he doesn't like having, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The napkins back under the register. Sixty. Wood setting the register down on them gently. Gully turning. 'What.' 'Nothing.' The strip has never lied in a balloon before. This is the first.

image.prompt: a young man gently setting a register back down on a stack of napkins as a teenager turns from a bait tank, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Sixty napkins. 'Nothing.' The strip's first lie in a balloon.
